_what: The styleProfile equivalent for our seven LIVE caption styles, read from src/remotion/src/captions/<Style>/<Style>.tsx — the defaults in each exported component's own signature, which is what renders when ChatCut supplies nothing. Not transcribed from the types.ts doc comments: a stale comment is read as fact by the next person, including the person who wrote it.

_canvas.note: fontSize values are px at this canvas; every style then applies its own shrink-to-fit

_safe_area.source: shared/captionPosition.ts CAPTION_PADDING — TikTok safe area; bottom 420 clears the caption/progress/nav drawer and sidesSafe 200 clears the right action rail

_why_gadzhi_first: It is our closest analogue to Story Yellow — one keyword lit in yellow on plain white — so a field-by-field comparison against that template is meaningful and any mismatch is about the SCHEMA rather than about a style with no counterpart. A style with no counterpart would make a schema failure and a design difference look the same.

TwoTone.note: the only style with a real stroke

Lumen.note: keyword switches to Playfair Display 400 at 1.3x; a shine word at 1.6x

Prime.note: special words switch to Playfair Display

Pulse.note: keyword at 1.25x with a glow off the highlight colour; recoloured off blue deliberately because Prime owns blue

Cove.note: boxed words switch to Playfair Display 400 at 1.8x

_font_availability.result: ALL FOUR of our caption families exist verbatim in their catalogue — no substitution is needed and none is stated.
_font_availability._our_stack_is_not_a_family_name: CAPTION_FONTS wraps each family as `<Family>, <Noto fallback>` for non-Latin coverage. ChatCut wants the CANONICAL FAMILY NAME verbatim, so the profiles below give the primary family alone. The Noto tail is ours and does not travel.

_key_spelling: THE VALUES ARE MEASURED; THE KEY NAMES ARE NOT MINE TO CHOOSE. B1 holds the styleProfile schema from the 27 presets with Story Yellow as the template, so these are field SEMANTICS and values, mapped onto that schema by him. Inventing key names is exactly how browse_library was read three times with three guessed keys, each miss recorded as measured-and-empty.

_one_line_names.CleanCut: CleanCut — plain white words for narration, explainers and text that must not steal focus
_one_line_names.Cove: Cove — words in a soft rounded box for busy shots, outdoor footage and low contrast
_one_line_names.Gadzhi: Gadzhi — one keyword lit in yellow on two-word lines for punchlines and key terms
_one_line_names.Lumen: Lumen — a bright band behind the line for hype, reveals and high-energy delivery
_one_line_names.Prime: Prime — two stacked lines in white and blue for setups, payoffs and question-answer beats
_one_line_names.Pulse: Pulse — the whole line fades in for calm delivery, storytelling and slow reveals
_one_line_names.TwoTone: TwoTone — every word outlined in a second colour for punchy, loud and meme-style beats
